Category: Policy
Id: pol_attendance
Name: Attendance Policy
Location:
Contact:
Description: Parul University mandates a minimum attendance of 75% in each subject for a student to be eligible to appear in the semester-end examinations. Attendance is calculated subject-wise, not overall. A student who fails to maintain 75% attendance in any subject will not be permitted to sit for the examination in that subject and will be marked as detained. Students with attendance between 65% and 74% may apply for attendance condonation on medical or valid grounds by submitting supporting documents to the respective HOD and the Exam Section within the notified deadline. Condonation is not a right and is granted at the discretion of the university. Students with attendance below 65% in any subject are not eligible for condonation and will be detained. Attendance is marked through the university's digital attendance system in most departments. Students must ensure their attendance is being recorded correctly and report discrepancies to their faculty immediately. Proxy attendance is a punishable offense and may lead to disciplinary action including rustication. Medical leave, participation in university-approved events, and sports representation with prior permission from the HOD may be considered for attendance relaxation on a case-by-case basis.

metadata.content: Parul University mandates a minimum attendance of 75% in each subject for a student to be eligible to appear in the semester-end examinations. Attendance is calculated subject-wise, not overall. A student who fails to maintain 75% attendance in any subject will not be permitted to sit for the examination in that subject and will be marked as detained. Students with attendance between 65% and 74% may apply for attendance condonation on medical or valid grounds by submitting supporting documents to the respective HOD and the Exam Section within the notified deadline. Condonation is not a right and is granted at the discretion of the university. Students with attendance below 65% in any subject are not eligible for condonation and will be detained. Attendance is marked through the university's digital attendance system in most departments. Students must ensure their attendance is being recorded correctly and report discrepancies to their faculty immediately. Proxy attendance is a punishable offense and may lead to disciplinary action including rustication. Medical leave, participation in university-approved events, and sports representation with prior permission from the HOD may be considered for attendance relaxation on a case-by-case basis.

Name: Hostel Rules and Regulations
Location:
Contact:
Description: All hostel residents of Parul University must adhere to the following rules and regulations. Students must return to the hostel by 10:00 PM. Any student wishing to stay out beyond this time must obtain prior written permission from the warden and inform their parents or guardians. Boys are not permitted in girls' hostels and vice versa under any circumstance. Violation of this rule will result in immediate disciplinary action. Guests including family members are permitted only in the common area of the hostel and must be registered at the hostel reception. Guests are not permitted to stay overnight in the hostel rooms. Alcohol, tobacco, drugs, and smoking are strictly prohibited anywhere within the hostel premises. Possession or consumption of prohibited substances will lead to immediate expulsion from the hostel and may result in rustication from the university. Students must maintain cleanliness of their rooms and common areas. Ragging in any form is a cognizable offense and is strictly prohibited. Any instance of ragging must be reported to the warden, the Anti-Ragging Committee, or the hostel superintendent immediately. Loud music, creating disturbance, or engaging in activities that disrupt the peace of other residents is prohibited between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM. Electrical appliances including irons, heaters, and hotplates are not permitted in hostel rooms due to fire safety regulations. Students must keep their rooms locked when not in use. The university is not responsible for theft of personal belongings. Any maintenance issues in the room must be reported to the warden in writing. Students wishing to vacate the hostel must submit a no-dues clearance from the hostel office before leaving.

Name: Library Rules and Regulations
Location:
Contact:
Description: The Central Library at Parul University is open to all enrolled students, faculty, and staff. University ID card or Library card is mandatory for entry into the library. Personal belongings including bags must be deposited at the bag counter before entering. Only transparent bags or files are permitted inside the library. Strict silence must be maintained inside the library at all times. Mobile phones must be switched to silent mode. Phone calls must not be made inside the library. Food, beverages, and chewing gum are strictly not permitted inside the library premises. A student can borrow a maximum of 3 books at a time for a period of 15 days. Books can be renewed once if no other student has reserved them. Books not returned by the due date will attract a fine of Rs. 2 per day per book. Books can be renewed at the counter or through the library portal. Students who lose a library book must replace it with the same edition or pay the cost of the book plus a penalty as determined by the librarian. Reference books, journals, newspapers, and project reports cannot be taken out of the library and must be read inside only. Marking, underlining, or damaging library books is a punishable offense. The library has a dedicated digital section with computers providing access to e-journals, NPTEL, INFLIBNET, and other online resources. Use of library computers for personal social media or non-academic purposes is not permitted.

Name: Student Code of Conduct
Location:
Contact:
Description: Parul University expects all students to maintain the highest standards of conduct and discipline on campus. Students must carry their university ID card at all times within the campus premises. The university follows a formal dress code. Students are expected to dress modestly and professionally. Sleeveless tops, shorts, torn jeans, and revealing clothing are not permitted in academic buildings and administrative offices. Proper footwear must be worn at all times. Ragging in any form — physical, verbal, psychological, or online — is a cognizable offense under the UGC Anti-Ragging regulations and the Supreme Court directives. Any student found guilty of ragging will be expelled from the university and a police complaint will be filed. Students must treat all faculty, staff, and fellow students with respect. Use of abusive language, harassment, or intimidation is a serious disciplinary offense. Students must not engage in any political activity, demonstration, or procession within the campus without prior permission from university authorities. Vandalism, destruction of university property, or tampering with fire safety equipment is a criminal offense. Students must not engage in any activity that brings disrepute to the university including misconduct on social media directed at the institution or its members. Smoking and consumption of tobacco products anywhere on campus is strictly prohibited. Vehicles on campus must be parked only in designated parking zones and driven at a safe speed. Rash driving or use of vehicles without a valid license is prohibited. Disciplinary action for misconduct ranges from a written warning to suspension, rustication, and police complaint depending on the severity of the offense.

Description: Parul University has a zero-tolerance policy against ragging in compliance with UGC Anti-Ragging Regulations and the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India directives. Any student found guilty of ragging will face immediate expulsion from the university, cancellation of admission, and a police complaint. The university has an active Anti-Ragging Committee and Anti-Ragging Squad that conducts regular checks especially during the first weeks of a new academic year. Students who experience or witness ragging must report it immediately to the warden, Anti-Ragging Committee member, or the university Anti-Ragging Helpline. Complaints can also be made on the national anti-ragging helpline number 1800-180-5522 or at www.antiragging.in. All ragging complaints are treated with complete confidentiality. Fresher students are advised to report any uncomfortable situation immediately without fear. All students must submit an anti-ragging undertaking at the time of admission each year.

Name: Parul University Foundation, History & Founders
Location:
Contact:
Description: The story of Parul University begins in 1989 when Dr. Parul Patel's father established the Parul Arogya Seva Mandal (PASM) Trust with the mission of advancing education, social welfare, and healthcare. The university and trust are named after Dr. Parul Patel. Dr. Parul Patel holds an MD in Organon from Hemchandracharya North Gujarat University and served as Professor at Rajkot Homoeopathic Medical College before dedicating herself to institution-building. She founded the first academic institution under the trust, Ahmedabad Homeopathic College, in 1993. Dr. Parul Patel currently serves as Vice President (Student Affairs and General Administration) and Chair of the Admissions Committee. From 2008 onwards, President Dr. Devanshu Patel (MBBS, MD Pharmacology) spearheaded the university's multidisciplinary expansion, establishing institutes in Management, Physiotherapy, Engineering, Architecture, and Computer Applications, as well as the Parul Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (PIMSR) and the 750+ bed Parul Sevashram Hospital. In 2015, Parul University was formally established as a private university.
